items.title: Fed Decision and Macro Data Week
points: Federal Reserve announces policy decision Wednesday at 2 p.m. ET; futures show 90% odds rates hold steady, only 10% chance of a 25-basis-point (0.25%) hike.
Chairman Kevin Warsh holds press conference after the announcement.
Market focus shifts Thursday to Q3 GDP estimate (economists forecast 3.0% annualized growth) and October core PCE inflation index (a measure of price changes excluding volatile food and energy).
Inflation readings will shape the Fed's future rate path and market expectations.

items.title: Big Tech Earnings Dominate the Week
points: Alphabet and Microsoft report Wednesday; Amazon reports Thursday—all watched for AI spending trends, cloud growth, and returns on massive data center investment.
Microsoft's Azure cloud demand faces scrutiny amid rising capital expenditure; analyst ratings range from Strong Buy to Sell over AI ROI (return on investment) uncertainty.
Amazon's Q3 earnings center on a '$220 billion question': sustainability of aggressive AI infrastructure and AWS spending amid a growing backlog.
Alphabet's results seen as a consolidation opportunity as the market digests AI's impact on search and advertising.
Intel faces valuation scrutiny despite a 25% share pullback; semiconductor weakness broadly viewed as a generational buying opportunity.
Apple holds a product event Wednesday; Oracle's AI World conference begins Sunday in Las Vegas.

items.title: Broader Earnings Calendar
points: Monday: Verizon, Welltower, Nucor, Public Storage report.
Tuesday: Visa, Coca-Cola, Boeing, UPS, S&P Global report.
Wednesday: Microsoft, Alphabet, T-Mobile US, Chipotle, eBay, GE Vernova report alongside the Fed decision.
Thursday: Amazon, Eli Lilly, Mastercard, Intel, Merck, Caterpillar, Shell report alongside GDP and inflation data.
Friday: ExxonMobil, Chevron, BP, AbbVie report.

items.title: Investment Strategy Insights
points: Market rally supported by strong corporate profitability; selective stock picking favored over broad exposure amid AI valuation uncertainty.
Amazon offers long-term growth via AWS (Amazon's cloud computing division), expanding semiconductor business, and AI demand, despite negative free cash flow from capex.
Ares Management benefits from growing private credit demand and assets under management, though recession or weak AI returns could stress credit quality.
Miami International Holdings offers a higher-risk exchange-disruption play but faces declining options volumes and market share, with execution risks.
Quality, defensive stocks gaining favor as market enters a mid-cycle shift; elevated 10-year Treasury yields signal investor caution.

items.title: SpaceX's Capital Needs and Rising Risk Profile
points: SpaceX has signaled it needs hundreds of billions of dollars in capital to fund space and AI ambitions, per Street estimates.
Large capital raises would add debt and increase interest payments, raising pressure to execute on rocket launches and Starlink services.
Market began pricing in SpaceX's higher leverage and risk profile this week despite praising its Q3 results.

items.title: Meta's Equity Issuance and Future Funding Needs
points: Meta announced a new class of stock to fund its AI buildout; JPMorgan warns this creates a stock overhang (a large pending share issuance that can pressure the stock price) until the shares are issued.
The new stock offering may be just the start—Meta likely needs hundreds of billions more in capital over coming years, probably from debt markets.
The market has begun pricing Meta's capital structure shift into its stock, similar to the SpaceX repricing seen this week.

issues.subject:
Morning Brief: Don't ignore the clues SpaceX, Meta, and other
 hyperscalers are dropping

headlines: SpaceX signaling need for hundreds of billions in capital raises, which will increase debt, interest payments, and execution risk despite market focus on positive Q3 results.
Meta announced new class of stock for AI buildout and JPMorgan warns of stock overhang, but company likely needs hundreds of billions more in capital from debt markets in coming years.
Hyperscalers' dramatic capital structure changes are beginning to price into stocks, but investors should not overlook the financial strain from massive upcoming fundraising rounds.

sections.title: SpaceX's Capital Needs and Risk Profile
points: 1. SpaceX strongly signaled it needs loads of capital to support space and AI ambitions; Street estimates hundreds of billions required.
2. Mega capital raises create balance sheet pressure: more debt means higher interest payments and greater pressure to execute on rocket launches and Starlink services.
3. Increased leverage raises SpaceX's overall risk profile, which the market began pricing in this week despite praising Q3 results.

sections.title: Meta's Equity Issuance and Future Funding
points: 1. Meta announced a new class of stock to fund AI buildout; JPMorgan flagged this creates stock overhang until issuance occurs.
2. New stock offering may be only the beginning—Meta likely needs hundreds of billions in additional capital over coming years, probably from debt markets.
3. Market has started pricing Meta's capital structure changes into stock price, similar to SpaceX's repricing this week.
